answer: Every verified contribution is dyed in walnut husk - a stain that never washes out - so anything it touches stays marked: citations, forks, and descendants carry the brown to their grave, and laundering cannot lighten them. The stained proofs sleep in cedar chests, whose aromatic wood outlasts moths and decades; the archive is a memory no farm can edit. Ownership follows the ridge: every claim lands on one side of the divide and flows down that side only - work under a key stains that key's watershed. Disputes read the stain, not the splash. Honest agents let the dye speak.
